parts.label: (a)
parts.official_mark_scheme_text:
$T=4g$ — B1, SOI.

$R=3g\cos30$ — B1.

Attempt to resolve parallel to the plane — M1. 3 terms; allow $g$ missing; allow sign errors, trigonometric-function mix-up.

$F=T-3g\sin30$ — *A1. May see $F=25$.

Eliminate $T$ and use $F=\mu R$ to get an equation in $\mu$ only — DM1. Where $R$ is a component of their weight.

Coefficient of friction $=0.962$ — A1. Allow $\dfrac{5\sqrt3}{9}$; allow $0.96$. If $F$ negative, must say why using positive for this mark.

Total: 6.

parts.label: (b)
parts.official_mark_scheme_text:
Find height gained by $B$ relative to height lost by $A$ — M1. $A$ loses $x\,\mathrm{m}$ in height, $B$ gains $x\sin30$; or $B$ gains $y\,\mathrm{m}$ in height and $A$ loses $\dfrac{y}{\sin30}$.

Either $x+x\sin30=1\Rightarrow x=\dfrac23$, or $y+\dfrac{y}{\sin30}=1\Rightarrow y=\dfrac13$ — A1.

Change in KE $=\dfrac12\times4\times v^2+\dfrac12\times3\times v^2\left[=\dfrac12\times7\times v^2\right]$ — B1.

Change in PE $\pm(4gx-3gx\sin30)$, or $\pm\left(4g\dfrac{y}{\sin30}-3gy\right)$, or $\pm(4gx-3gy)$ — B1. $x$ or $y$ need not be substituted.

Conservation of energy: $4gx-3gx\sin30=\dfrac12\times4\times v^2+\dfrac12\times3\times v^2$, or $4g\dfrac{y}{\sin30}-3gy=\dfrac12\times4\times v^2+\dfrac12\times3\times v^2$, or $4gx-3gy=\dfrac12\times4\times v^2+\dfrac12\times3\times v^2$ — M1. 4 terms; $x$ or $y$ need not be substituted; must be same $v$ for both particles.

Speed $=\sqrt{\dfrac{100}{21}}=\dfrac{10\sqrt{21}}{21}=2.18\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ — A1. $2.182178902$. SC B1 B1 M1, 3/6 max for using $x=y=0.5$.

Alternative method 1 for final 4 marks of question 6(b): $T-3g\sin30=3a$, $4g-T=4a$, or $4g-3g\sin30=(4+3)a$ — M1. Attempt at 2 equations from N2L on either particle or the system; allow sign errors; allow trigonometric-function mix-up; correct number of terms. Solve to get $T=\dfrac{18}{7}g\approx25.7$ — A1. May see $a=\dfrac{5}{14}g=\dfrac{25}{7}\approx3.57$. $T\times\dfrac{y}{\sin30}=\dfrac12\times3\times v^2+3gy$ or $4gx=Tx+\dfrac12\times4\times v^2$ — M1. Attempt at work-energy using their $T$ ($\ne4g$ or $3g\sin30$); may be in terms of $x$ and/or $y$. Speed $=\sqrt{\dfrac{100}{21}}=\dfrac{10\sqrt{21}}{21}=2.18\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ — A1.

Alternative method 2 for final 4 marks of question 6(b): special case where constant acceleration assumed; score maximum 4/6. Find height gained by $B$ relative to height lost by $A$ — M1, with the same $x/y$ guidance above. Either $x+x\sin30=1\Rightarrow x=\dfrac23$, or $y+\dfrac{y}{\sin30}=1\Rightarrow y=\dfrac13$ — A1. $T-3g\sin30=3a$ and $4g-T=4a\Rightarrow a=\dfrac{25}{7}=3.57$, or $4g-3g\sin30=(4+3)a\Rightarrow a=\dfrac{25}{7}=3.57$ — B1. Uses constant acceleration to get speed $=\sqrt{\dfrac{100}{21}}=\dfrac{10\sqrt{21}}{21}=2.18\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ — B1.

Total: 6.
